A1.justification: Both PDFs describe I2VControl-Camera and provide readable corresponding methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and references. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original generated-video examples and quantitative evaluations on RealEstate10K and movable-object samples in Section 4, Figures 5–7, and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains original qualitative video-generation results and quantitative camera-control, image-quality, and motion measurements in Section 4 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the reported trajectory-tracking component from CoTracker to SpatialTracker. The control representation, static/dynamic partitioning algorithm, adapter architecture, and training objective remain unchanged. The expanded inference description explains the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the collected training videos, RealEstate10K static scenes, synthetic movable-object samples featuring humans and animals, and WebVid reference frames for FID. The evaluated camera-motion scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl remain the evaluated baselines on both datasets, retrained using the same Magicvideo-V2 setup. AnimateDiff motion-LoRA remains excluded. The tracker substitution concerns the data pipeline, not comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported trajectory preprocessing changes from CoTracker to SpatialTracker in Section 3.3. Section 4.1 otherwise retains the sample counts, camera-motion sampling, metrics, 24-frame output, 704 × 448 resolution, and 20K-step training budget. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same controllability examples and motion-strength analyses remain: Figure 6 compares strengths 0 and 600, and Table 2 reports strengths 0, 200, 400, and 600. No ablation, robustness test, or additional case study is introduced or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Tables 1–2 retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are identical, including RealEstate10K Ours-0 RotErr 0.53 and TransErr 9.72, and movable-object Ours-600 FID 91.86. The qualitative examples and reported findings are also retained; no new outcome demonstrates an effect of the tracker substitution.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the same trajectory decomposition, Maclaurin argument, motion-strength definition, and fitting formulations. Algorithm 1 and the associated assumptions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introductory Figure 1 caption drops the explicit claim that the method supports 'any camera movement style.' This is a limited removal of a universal capability assertion; the abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the central claims about precise camera control, adjustable subject motion, and superiority over previous methods.

C2.justification: The interpretations of camera precision, adjustable dynamics, and higher Ours-0 FID on movable objects remain unchanged. The same drag and motion-brush extensions are proposed, with no new substantive limitation or failure condition.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page URL to the abstract and directs readers there for video results in Section 4.2. It also revises the named tracking dependency to SpatialTracker. Hardware and training details are retained; the PDFs do not establish a new code or dataset release.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces the VideoCrafter2 citation with Feng et al.'s I2VControl, while Section 3.3 replaces the CoTracker citation with SpatialTracker. The bibliography reflects these substitutions. The related-work discussion and broader research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.4 expands the inference explanation, the publication header changes from preprint to ICLR 2025, and the acknowledgement is removed. These are localized edits; the main section hierarchy and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All seven figures and both tables are retained. Figures 1–2 receive revised captions, Figures 3–4 shift relative to surrounding text, and spacing and page flow change. The illustrations, qualitative examples, and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 and Section 3.4 explain the existing depth-lifting, camera-coordinate transformation, and 2D-projection sequence more clearly, and the project-page pointer improves resource discoverability. These provide modest documentation gains. The empirical and theoretical evidence is unchanged, and no reported comparison establishes a benefit from the tracker substitution.
